subject: Order form indemnity — notice process, SLA exceptions, and insurance trigger
messages:
From: Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@luminara.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Luminara Procurement <procurement@luminara.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Order form — indemnity notice & evidence process

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the call earlier. Procurement/legal at Luminara have a couple of items we need to lock in before we can sign the order form:

- Notice timing: we need a definitive timeline for when Redwood must notify us and when we must respond to third-party IP claims (we typically ask for a 10 business day initial acknowledgement and 30 days for a substantive response).
- Evidence & privilege: what evidence will Redwood provide when a third-party claim is asserted (sample outputs, system logs)? We need clear steps for transfer of technical evidence while preserving privilege where appropriate.
- Defense control: Luminara wants the customer to retain control of the defense for third-party infringement claims arising from model output. We can consider a compromise but want explicit ability to select counsel if there’s a conflict.
- Insurance trigger: we'd like to see an explicit insurance-trigger threshold in the order form (e.g., when a claim exceeds $1M, Redwood must carry or trigger its insurance to cover defense costs).

Can you confirm Redwood’s preferred position on these points and share a redline of the order form with the notice/evidence language? We can then work with our external counsel to finalize.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is targeting sign by mid-June.

Best,
Sarah Hayes
Sr. Counsel, Luminara Inc.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Order form — indemnity notice & evidence process

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses below and I’m looping in Kim (Legal) and Ben (Sales) so we can produce a redline and an evidence checklist.

Summary of Redwood’s initial positions (high level):
- Notice timing: we can do 5 business days for initial acknowlegement and 30 calendar days for Redwood to investigate and provide a substantive response. We prefer calendar days for operational simplicity, but open to 30 business days if that’s a hard requirement.
- Evidence & privilege: Redwood can provide system logs, request/response payloads, and model inference metadata where available. We will redact privileged internal notes and preserve attorney-client communications. We propose an \"evidence handback\" process: Redwood curates evidence, places it in a secure share, and provides a single-point contact for Luminara to retrieve materials.
- Defense control: default Redwood position is defend-vs-reimburse for third-party IP claims related to the underlying model or service (not customer-provided content). We are willing to accept customer control in limited cases (e.g., where the alleged infringement is solely based on customer materials).
- Insurance trigger: Redwood carries commercial liability and cyber coverage; can commit to notifying when a claim exceeds $1M and to cooperate with insurer. We will propose a clause that requires an insurance-trigger notice to be sent at $1M and above; exact insurer sublimits to be redlined.

Next steps: Kim — can you draft a compact redline for the order form that: 1) codifies the notice/evidence handback process, 2) includes an insurance-trigger notification at $1M, and 3) proposes defend-vs-reimburse with carveouts for customer-supplied content. Ben — FYI on timing: Luminara wants mid-June sign.

I’m attaching the current order form and a starter evidence checklist (draft). If we can get a redline back in 48 hours I’ll route it to Luminara.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form — indemnity notice & evidence process

Soojin / Ben — drafting notes below (will convert to tracked redline and return today):

1) Notice windows
- I prefer 5 business days for initial acknowledgement, 30 calendar days for Redwood’s substantive response (we should state what constitutes a \"substantive response\").

2) Evidence handback
- Redwood will provide: sample outputs, request timestamps, inference IDs/KV cache metadata, and relevant config (model version, quantization profile) where available.
- Privilege carveout: Redwood will not produce internal privileged communications; where production could waive privilege, we will produce a privilege log and coordinate over a privilege review.

3) Defense control / counsel
- Compromise: Redwood will accept defense control by default but must have the right to assume control if Redwood reasonably believes there is a conflict or an indemnified claim would materially prejudice Redwood’s broader customer base. If customer insists on control, require their counsel to be reasonably acceptable to Redwood and require customer to fund any additional costs arising from their counsel’s decisions.

4) Monetary caps & insurance trigger
- Propose a cap equal to the greater of: (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (ii) $3,000,000.
- Insurance-trigger: require notification at $1,000,000 and reasonable cooperation with insurance defense. We should avoid a hard requirement that the insurer must "step in" unless the insurance policy language allows.

5) Operational SLA exceptions
- If Redwood needs additional time to gather logs/evidence due to retention windows, include a carveout allowing a limited extension with notice (e.g., up to 15 days) so we are not penalized for retention policy gaps.

I will prepare the tracked redline and an updated evidence checklist that maps each evidence item to our internal retention/availability expectations.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Hayes <sarah.hayes@luminara.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form — indemnity notice & evidence process

Kim / Soojin — thanks, this is helpful and closer to what we need. A few clarifications from Luminara:

- Defense control: Luminara will accept Redwood defending in the ordinary course, but reserves the right to step in if the claim directly implicates customer data or if Redwood’s chosen defense would expose Luminara to damages not covered by the defense strategy (we will propose an escalation panel clause).
- Cap: Luminara will push back on the $3M anchor; we will propose a sliding scale tied to ARR / contract value. That said, if Redwood can show $3M is standard in your peer set, we may accept it.
- Insurance: acceptable to keep the language flexible as long as we get a firm notification at $1M and a commitment to cooperate with insurers.
- Privilege: we need a detailed privilege log in any production that excludes privilege.

I will circulate Luminara’s procurement redline by EOD tomorrow with markup on the defense-control paragraph and a proposed sliding cap schedule.

One ask: can Redwood confirm who will be our technical point of contact for evidence retrieval? That will speed the operational handoff once a notice is triggered.

Regards,
Sarah Hayes
Sr. Counsel, Luminara Inc.

Thanks — appreciate the quick collaboration.
